script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 21. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Reptiles don't waste energy heating themselves—they let the sun do it.  This seems primitive, but it's actually efficient.  Cold-blooded animals need only 10% of the food mammals need.

Mammals burn 90% of their food just to stay warm. Reptiles use almost all their food for growth and activity. A crocodile can survive a year on what a lion eats in a week. Less input, comparable output. Crocodiles have barely changed in 80 million years—they watched dinosaurs come and go.  Their design works so well that evolution hasn't needed to improve it.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Efficiency often beats power.  Reptiles teach that using less can be an advantage.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Efficiency Thinking - Do More With Less.

Here's your activity: Identify one area of your life where you could 'go cold-blooded'—achieving the same result with less energy, less effort, or fewer resources. Sometimes the best solution isn't doing more, but needing less. This helps you apply efficiency thinking to life situations.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about cold-blooded survivors can be applied to efficiency thinking - do more with less. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
